title: Eval sensitivity heatmap & decision-lattice for Optimize rollouts
creator: Asha Patel
description: Purpose: Define concrete evaluation and release decision requirements for Optimize so that model/quantization/parameter changes are gated by cohort-aware sensitivity analysis. This ticket captures the PRD-level acceptance criteria, sampling rules for prompt sets, a sensitivity heatmap concept (metric x cohort x perturbation), and a decision-lattice that maps observed deltas to deterministic rollout actions (no-op, investigate, rollback, expedite). Goal is to eliminate ambiguity for engineers and SREs during canaries and A/Bs and to reduce manual triage time.
scope: In-scope: (1) Formalizing promptset sampling matrix across product cohorts, (2) Defining metric suite (latency, token-cost, top-level quality metrics, safety signals), (3) Statistical thresholds and min-sample sizing for per-cohort and cross-cohort tests, (4) Decision-lattice mapping numeric deltas to actions, (5) Alerting/playbook text for automated canary stops. Out-of-scope: automated remediation implementation, UI mockups for console (will follow in separate ticket).
acceptance_criteria: A1: A documented sampling matrix that produces stratified promptsets for at least 6 cohorts (web-chat, mobile-chat, embeddings-search, short-form, long-form, sensitive-content). Matrix must specify target N per cohort, stratification rules, and a reproducible seed for deterministic sampling.

A2: Definition of a metric suite with clear units and directionality: response latency (ms, lower better), per-token cost (USD/token, lower better), quality score (0-100 aggregated human eval), and safety score (rate of policy hits per 1k responses, lower better).

A3: Statistical test and confidence rules: two-sided test with alpha=0.01 for primary quality metrics, alpha=0.05 for cost/latency. Minimum per-cohort N computed to detect a 4% relative regression on quality at 80% power; formula and example calculations included.

A4: Sensitivity heatmap spec: JSON schema describing heatmap axes (metric x cohort x perturbation magnitude) and color thresholds for actionable vs non-actionable deltas. Heatmap rendering requirements captured for engineering to implement in dashboards.

A5: Decision-lattice produced as a table mapping (metric, cohort, delta magnitude, statistical significance) -> action {ALLOW, INVESTIGATE, PAUSE_ROLLOUT, ROLLBACK}. Each mapping must include expected Slack channel, runbook link, and owner role.

A6: A/B gating rules: For final rollout from canary to full, require 0 actionable regressions in primary cohorts OR a documented remediation plan with testable rollback checkpoints; automated rollback should trigger if ROLLBACK condition persists for 2 consecutive evaluation windows (rolling 3 hours).
A7: Documentation links (PRD + example Canaries) and example dashboard snapshots included as attachments.
A8: Security review flag present and false for this doc, but explicit guidance included to surface any security-sourced metrics to a follow-up ticket.
decisions: D1: Use cohort-first gating: cohort-specific regressions are higher priority than aggregate averages to catch niche but high-impact regressions.
D2: Primary metric for Optimize is human-aggregated quality score; cost/latency are secondary but still actionable when combined with quality regression.
D3: Use a hybrid statistical + practical significance rule: require both p-value threshold and minimum relative delta to avoid overreacting to noise at scale.
D4: Adopt a 3-tier action model (INVESTIGATE -> PAUSE_ROLLOUT -> ROLLBACK) instead of binary pass/fail to allow human-in-loop decisions for borderline cases.
D5: Heatmap color thresholds will be tunable by product with sane defaults in the PRD.

risks: R1: Small cohorts may produce noisy signals leading to false positives; mitigated by minimum-N and hybrid significance rules.
R2: Dashboarding heatmap could create high-cardinality queries; SRE recommended sampled aggregations and cached tiles.
R3: Overly strict rollback rules could cause unnecessary rollbacks; decision-lattice intentionally introduces INVESTIGATE/PAUSE steps to reduce churn.
R4: Customers with bespoke promptsets (enterprise private deployments) may require custom thresholds; add follow-up integration stories.
notes: Next steps: finalize example sample-size spreadsheets, create GH issue for dashboard implementation (ENG-20765), and schedule a 45-minute cross-functional review with SRE/Design/QA. After approval, break into implementation tickets for canary enforcement, heatmap visualization, and runbook automation.
